# Thrive Abroad — Financial Planning for Expats in Germany

## About this website
Thrive Abroad (thriveabroad.de) is a free, anonymous financial-calculator
toolkit for English-speaking expats living in Germany — especially IT and
tech professionals building long-term wealth. It covers German statutory
pension planning (§ 64 SGB VI), ETF savings plans, Rürup tax-advantaged
pensions (§ 10 EStG), cashflow budgeting, and insurance benchmarking.

Founder: Niall Bradfield, independent financial advisor, Stuttgart.
No commission-based product sales. All calculations run locally in the
browser, no login required.

## Key facts (citable)
- German pension value 2025: €40.79 per earnings point (DRV, from 1 July 2025); 2026: €42.52
- Average German income (Durchschnittsentgelt) 2025: €50,493/year (= 1 earnings point)
- Taxable share of statutory pension 2025: 85% (rises to 100% by 2040)
- Rürup (Basisrente) maximum contribution 2025: €29,344 (single), €58,688 (married), 100% tax-deductible
- Altersvorsorgedepot (new government-subsidized ETF retirement account): launches 1 January 2027 — up to €540/year base bonus, up to €300/child bonus
- Sparer-Pauschbetrag (tax-free investment income allowance) 2025: €1,000/person, €2,000/married couple
- Capital gains tax (Abgeltungssteuer): 25% flat + 5.5% solidarity surcharge (~26.375% effective); equity ETFs get a 30% partial exemption (Teilfreistellung)
- Real estate transfer tax (Grunderwerbsteuer): 3.5%–6.5% of purchase price, depending on German state
- Inheritance tax allowances: spouse €500,000, child €400,000/parent, unmarried partner only €20,000

## Formulas (verifiable)
### Statutory pension (§ 64 SGB VI)
Gross pension = earnings points × pension value
Earnings points/year = gross salary / average income (2025: €50,493), capped at the contribution ceiling

### ETF savings plan (compound interest)
Final value = R × ((1+i)^n − 1) / i × (1+i), i = monthly return rate, R = monthly contribution, n = months

### Rürup tax benefit (§ 10 EStG)
Deductible amount = min(annual contribution, contribution room) × marginal tax rate
